newsitem.title: CAPE VERDE: Cement plant to be built on Cape Verde-sources.
newsitem.headline: Cement plant to be built on Cape Verde-sources.

text.p: Construction of a cement manufacturer is expected to begin in the West African Cape Verde archipelago this year, government sources said.
The project on Maio island may include the participation of Portuguese cement firm Cimpor-Cimentos de Portugal, but Cimpor has yet to take a final decision, the sources said.
Cimpor, Portugal's largest cement producer, has said it had completed a study into the possibility of establishing the plant.

Cimpor sources said the company was expected to take a final decision on whether to join the project during a visit to the archipelago by Portuguese Prime Minister Antonio Guterres between February 16 and 20.
According to the plans, the cement plant on Maio, expected to start operations in 2000, would produce 200,000 tonnes of cement per year between 2000 and 2005.
The plant, expected to employ 135 people, would serve the domestic market and any excess production would be exported, the government sources said. Presently Cape Verde imports all its cement needs.
